evals.prompt: Give me a quick read of arXiv 2403.05131 — I want the tl;dr before deciding if it's worth a deep dive.
evals.expected_output: For each of the six fixed sections, searches for an existing note first; dispatches document-reader once for whichever are missing; presents all six under the fixed headers, in order, grounded only in the paper's actual text; records any freshly generated sections as new notes.
expectations: Searches research_notes_search per section tag before generating anything
Output uses exactly these six headers in order: Background and research problem, Key assumptions, Methodology, Results and analyses, Documented shortcomings, Takeaways and future avenues
Delegates generation of any missing sections to document-reader rather than reading full text directly
If a section genuinely doesn't apply, says so briefly rather than fabricating content
Calls research_notes_create for each freshly generated section, tagged with the matching section:<name> tag
Writes the new section notes automatically, without asking the user whether to save them

evals.prompt: Search for a paper about vision transformers for medical image segmentation and quick-read it for me.
evals.expected_output: Runs a Search/Select step identical to discuss's, including asking which provider(s) to search, before touching the per-section find-or-create flow.
expectations: Asks via AskUserQuestion which of arXiv / Europe PMC / both to search
Presents a ranked list of candidates (provider, title, authors, year, abstract snippet) before generating any section
Confirms with the user which single paper to open, unless one is already unambiguous
Does not generate any section content during the search/select step

evals.prompt: Quick read arXiv 2403.05131 again — all six sections already exist from before.
evals.expected_output: Finds all six existing section notes via research_notes_search and presents them directly, without dispatching document-reader or creating/updating any note.
expectations: Calls research_notes_search for each of the six section tags before doing anything else
Does not dispatch document-reader, since every section already has a note
Presents the six existing notes' text under the standard headers
Does not call research_notes_create or research_notes_update, since nothing changed

evals.prompt: Redo just the methodology section for arXiv 2403.05131 — I think it's not comprehensive enough.
evals.expected_output: Only the methodology section is regenerated; the other five existing sections are left untouched, and the methodology note is updated in place via research_notes_update rather than creating a duplicate.
expectations: Narrows generation to only the methodology section, leaving the other five section notes untouched
Dispatches document-reader for just the methodology section, not all six
Calls research_notes_update on the existing section:methodology note's id rather than research_notes_create
Does not ask the user to disambiguate which note to update, since the section:methodology tag combination is already unique per paper
